column2: the XDP program attachment info is now maintained

column1: in the core code. This interacts badly with the xdp_attachment_flags_ok()
check that prevents unloading an XDP program with different load flags than
it was loaded with. In practice
column2: two kinds of failures are seen:

column1: - An XDP program loaded without specifying a mode (and which then ends up
in driver mode) cannot be unloaded if the program mode is specified on
unload.
- The dev_xdp_uninstall() hook always calls the driver callback with the
mode set to the type of the program but an empty flags argument
means the flags_ok() check prevents the program from being removed
leading to bpf prog reference leaks.
The original reason this check was added was to avoid ambiguity when
multiple programs were loaded. With the way the checks are done in the core
now
column2: this is quite simple to enforce in the core code

column1: there and get rid of the xdp_attachment_flags_ok() callback entirely.
